name: Embraer 195
sources: [E190] Embraer APM-1901, Embraer 190 Airport Planning Manual, Revision 19 (27 August 2021) https://web.archive.org/web/20241008225620/https://www.embraercommercialaviation.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/APM_190.pdf: overall length 36.24 m (118 ft 11 in), span over winglets 28.72 m, pressurized section 29.08 m (2.2, p.2-2, 2-3); nose gear 4.13 m aft of the nose, wheelbase 13.83 m, track 5.94 m, forward cargo door 6.82 m and aft cargo door 24.57 m from the nose, forward doors 4.27 m (right) and 4.71 m (left), aft doors 27.60 m, the winglet's aft end 20.04 m, tailplane span 12.08 m, height 10.57 m (fig 2.1, p.2-4); the forward passenger door's centre line 5.18 m from the nose (fig 2.2 sheet 3, p.2-7).

[E195] Embraer APM-1997, Embraer 195 Airport Planning Manual, Revision 11 (09 October 2015) https://web.archive.org/web/20241008225517/https://www.embraercommercialaviation.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/02/APM_E195.pdf: overall length 38.67 m (126 ft 10 in), span over winglets 28.72 m (2.2.1, p.2-2); fuselage total length 38.65 m (126 ft 10 in), pressurized section 31.49 m (2.2.3, p.2-3); wheelbase 14.64 m, track 5.94 m, forward cargo door 6.82 m and aft cargo door 26.98 m from the nose, forward doors 4.27 m (right) and 4.71 m (left), aft doors 30.01 m, tailplane span 12.09 m, height 10.57 m (fig 2.1, p.2-4).

Fuselage: neither document prints a plug length. Both give each ground servicing connection's station (COORD. X, mm aft of the nose: the nose gear's jack point is at 4125 mm, and fig 2.1 has the nose gear 4.13 m from the nose): [E190] fig 5.4, p.5-7 and [E195] fig 5.4, p.5-7. The five connections on the nose do not move (nose gear jack point 4125.32 and 4125.04, steering switch 4136.97, 115 VAC power 4146.90, forward headset 4164.44, oxygen panel 6562.14). The twelve on the wing and the centre section each move 812.80 mm (air conditioning 13268.52 to 14081.32, pressure refuelling panel 17316.95 to 18129.75, hydraulic panels 1 and 2 20139.16 to 20951.96; the main gear jack points 18078.03 to 18890.21, 812.18 mm). The five behind the wing each move 2413.00 mm (water panel 27861.83 to 30274.83, waste panel 28784.01 to 31197.01, aft headset 30562.26 to 32975.26). Thus 0.81 m (32 in) more ahead of the wing, between the forward cargo door (6.82 m on both) and the air conditioning connection, and 2.413 - 0.813 = 1.60 m (63 in) more behind it, between the hydraulic panels and the aft cargo door.

The dimensions agree. Wheelbase 14.64 - 13.83 = 0.81 m, the nose gear in its place. Aft doors 30.01 - 27.60 = 2.41 m, aft cargo door 26.98 - 24.57 = 2.41 m, pressurized section 31.49 - 29.08 = 2.41 m.

The rest: foreM + aftM = 2.41 m; the two overall lengths differ by 38.67 - 36.24 = 2.43 m, 0.02 m more. [E195] prints the length as 38.67 m (2.2.1, fig 2.1) and as 38.65 m (2.2.3), each time as 126 ft 10 in; [E190] has 118 ft 11 in. In feet the difference is 7 ft 11 in = 95 in = 2.413 m, which is what every station gives: the 38.67 m is a rounding.

Doors: the E195 has the E190's doors, moved with the fuselage. The same nose and the same forward doors (4.27 m and 4.71 m on both); the aft doors 2.41 m further aft; a passenger door ahead of the wing and one behind it on the left, a service door opposite each, and one overwing emergency exit on each side (the side and plan views of fig 2.1 and the ground clearance tables, [E190] table 2.2, p.2-9, [E195] table 2.2, p.2-6). No stations of its own.

Wingtip: the same wing and winglets. Span over winglets 28.72 m, wing reference area 92.50 m2 and aspect ratio 8.1 on both ([E190] 2.2, [E195] 2.2); the winglet's top 5.09 m (E190) and 5.08 m (E195) above the ground at the maximum ramp weight (table 2.2). No change.

Nacelles: two GE CF34-10 of 82.3 kN on both ([E190] 2.1, p.2-1; [E195] 2.1, p.2-1); the nacelle 0.49 m above the ground at the maximum ramp weight on both (table 2.2); the engine's connections move with the wing (engine air starting 13629.01 to 14441.81 mm, fig 5.4). No change.

Gear: [E190] fig 7.1, p.7-2 and [E195] fig 7.1, p.7-2: two wheels on each leg, nose tyres 24 x 7.7 16PR, main tyres H41 x 16-20 22PR, main wheels 0.87 m apart and nose wheels 0.40 m apart, track 5.94 m on both. Only the wheelbase differs: 14.64 m = 13.83 + 0.81 m. The base's gear is kept.

The E195-E2 (E295) is drawn on this model. [E2] Embraer APM-5824, E-Jets E2 Airport Planning Manual, Revision 25 (29 November 2024) https://web.archive.org/web/20250706172127/https://www.embraercommercialaviation.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/06/E-JETS-E2_APM_E-JetsE2-1.pdf, 2.2.2 (section 2, p.4) and fig 2.2 (section 2, p.7): overall length 41.60 m, 2.93 m more than the E195; span 35.12 m over swept-back wingtips, no winglets (the wingtip 3.90 m above the ground, table 2.7); a new wing of 103 m2; nose gear 4.55 m aft of the nose, wheelbase 15.71 m, track 6.73 m; forward doors 4.27 m and 4.71 m as on the E195, aft doors 32.87 m (2.86 m more), aft cargo door 29.83 m; tailplane span 10.0 m; two PW1921G, the nacelle 0.37 m above the ground. Fig 7.2 (section 7, p.3): two wheels on each leg, nose tyres H27x8.5R12, main tyres H42x16.0R20. The same fuselage section and door layout, with two overwing exits on each side; this model shows it 2.93 m too short, with the E195's wing, winglets, engines and gear.
